title: Lean-Formalized Proof of the 1960 Erdős–Rado Fixed-Petal Sunflower Conjecture
whyItMatters: Claims an exponential B_r^k upper bound settling the 66-year-old Erdős–Rado Sunflower Conjecture for every fixed petal count r ≥ 3, accompanied by a Lean 4 formalization.
summary: Posed by Paul Erdős and Richard Rado in 1960, the Sunflower Conjecture asks whether every family of more than C_r^k sets of size k contains an r-sunflower (r sets with identical pairwise intersections). Following the landmark 2019 Alweiss–Lovett–Wu–Zhang (log k)^k breakthrough, OpenAI’s November 24 preprint applies Euclidean geometry of the asymptotic spectrum of tensors to remove the log-factor barrier completely, proving an exponential bound B_r^k with Lean 4 formalization of the fixed-petal theorem.
technicalHighlights: Proves that for every r ≥ 3, more than B_r^k sets of size ≤ k force an r-sunflower, with log B_r = O((log r)^4 (log log 2r)^(5/2)).
Accompanied by a Lean 4 formalization (FixedBase.lean) proving existence of the exponential base C_r for every r ≥ 3.
Demonstrates unexpected transfer from algebraic tensor-spectrum geometry directly into extremal combinatorics.
caveats: Unreviewed November 24 preprint; the Lean file formalizes existence of C_r while the sharper quantitative dependence of B_r on r appears in the manuscript and awaits independent combinatorial refereeing.

scoreRationale.foundational: Settles one of Paul Erdős’s most famous and widely cited 1960 conjectures in extremal combinatorics.
scoreRationale.ripple: Sunflower lemmas are core tools in circuit complexity, pseudorandomness, data structures, and matrix multiplication.
scoreRationale.verification: Includes a Lean 4 proof of the fixed-base exponential theorem, awaiting independent review of both Lean definitions and quantitative manuscript bounds.
scoreRationale.velocity: Bridged the final gap from the 2019 (log k)^k bound to the full exponential conjecture via AI-developed tensor geometry.
